findings.evidence: "C35-004/005 Faculty class aggregates round twice (... a mean of 12.5% shown as 12%)". C35-005 is not double rounding: it is a floating-point artefact at an exact .5 (Math.round(100*sum/n) with sum 0.3749999...). Reproduced through the real API: class of 4 students on hem-01 with 1,2,2,2 wrong answers -> API missions[hem-01].successPct = 37 and hardestMission.successPct = 37, exact rational mean 37.5 (raw JS value 37.49999999999999) which half-up rounds to 38. Exhaustive check: 246 equal-mission combinations of 2-6 students with wrong <= 8 differ from exact half-up; 110,879 student-accuracy combinations over the 9 standard missions (wrong <= 5). Same family as A37-005 (competencies). A student-level flag threshold (59.5 vs 60) and the hardest-mission threshold (69.5 vs 70) can sit on the same boundary.
findings.fix_hint: Describe the cause correctly (float sum, one rounding) and say it can move a displayed percentage by 1 point and, at the 60/70 thresholds, a flag; fix with integer arithmetic.

findings.state_artifact: be/src/game.ts:1052-1055 (hardest mission) + be/README.md:68 + web UI "Needs attention" chip
findings.evidence: The hardest mission is chosen with reduce(b < a ? b : a) on the ROUNDED successPct, so ties keep the first mission in catalogue order. Deterministic, but the flagged mission is not the lowest one. Reproduced on class "UI Tie Class" (id 9; 3 students, hem-01 wrong answers 0,1,3 and hem-02 wrong answers 1,2,5): raw hem-01 = 58.33 (rounds 58), raw hem-02 = 57.5 (API 58); hardestMission = Blood Smear Code 58% and only that row carries "Needs attention"; Fix the Sample, the lower one, shows "accuracy 58%" unflagged. Documented rule says "the lowest mission is the hardest".
findings.fix_hint: Break ties on the unrounded mean (then on catalogue order) and mention the tie rule in be/README.
